tools.name: search_offers
tools.description: Search current AI model offers (one model at one provider = one offer) by words, model type and limits; priced offers first, doubtful prices after sane ones. Each row has offer_id, model_id, provider_id, prices in USD per 1M tokens (or per unit), card_url and a cite line. Next: get_card {"card_id":

tools.name: get_model_prices
tools.description: Every seller's current price of one model (an id, or a name to search for), cheapest input first.

tools.name: cheapest
tools.description: The cheapest current offers (rows: one model at one provider) of one model type, by input price. For the cheapest MODELS of a job (one row per model) use cheapest_models; for a monthly workload use cheapest_for_workload.

tools.name: compare_models
tools.description: 2 to 5 models side by side: the best current offer of each and, for up to 4, every field compared (lowest and median input/output price, context, max output, providers, regions, a 1M-in/200k-out workload cost), who wins by how many percent, providers selling all, and summary sentences.

tools.name: estimate_cost
tools.description: The cost of a workload (input, output and cached input tokens, number of requests) at every current provider of one model, cheapest first, in USD - what the same job costs where.

tools.name: get_card
tools.description: One card with its citation. card_id is '<kind>:<key>': offer:<provider>|<model id as the provider writes it> (e.g. offer:anthropic|claude-opus-4), model:<creator>/<model> (e.g. model:anthropic/claude-opus-4), seller:<provider key> (e.g. seller:anthropic). Ids come from search_offers (offer_id, model

tools.name: validate_provider_files
tools.description: For a provider (seller) joining the catalog: check a models.yaml before putting it online - the same check as the wizard and POST /v1/provider/validate. Give the file's text in `models` (YAML, or the same structure as JSON text); `domain` (the provider's site) makes the model_page checks exact. Retu

tools.name: cheapest_for_workload
tools.description: The cheapest offers for a whole monthly workload, ranked by monthly cost in USD: give a preset (a typical job; see workload_presets) and/or your own tokens a month. Best offer of each model; free promos and batch/flex/priority/regional prices left out unless asked. Each row: monthly_cost_usd, prices

tools.name: workload_presets
tools.description: The ready-made workloads of cheapest_for_workload: name, what job it is, tokens a month, context needed, model type.

tools.name: list_articles
tools.description: AI Rate Card's articles on AI model prices (the cheapest models by task, price moves, costs), newest first, with their links - to quote or point a reader to.

tools.name: cheapest_models
tools.description: The n cheapest MODELS for a job (task): each model counted once at its own lowest current price (input tokens by default). One row per model with that price, where it is and card_url.

tools.name: dearest_models
tools.description: The n most expensive MODELS for a job (task): each model counted once at its own lowest current price, highest first - the top of the market. Same arguments as cheapest_models.

tools.name: median_models
tools.description: The typical (median) current price of a job (task) across models, and the n models closest to it - what a normal price for this job is. Same arguments as cheapest_models.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: validate_provider_files · Private data: search_offers, estimate_cost, validate_provider_files, cheapest_for_workload, workload_presets, cheapest_models · Public sink: validate_provider_files.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: validate_provider_files · Private data: search_offers, estimate_cost, validate_provider_files, cheapest_for_workload, workload_presets, cheapest_models · Public sink: validate_provider_files

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
